For Applicant : Shri Hemant Agrawal, Advocate For Respondent/State : Smt. Usha Chandrakar, Pl
Hon'ble Shri Justice Sachin Singh Rajput C A V Order 20/01/2023
1.

The applicant has filed this application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for
grant of regular bail as he is in custody in connection with Crime No. 17/2022 registered at police
station Chhawani, District Durg (Cg) for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) and
506 Ipc and Sections 5 & 6 of the Pocso Act.
2.
Case of the prosecution in brief is that the applicant developed physical relation with the prosecutrix, who is aged about 18 years, on the pretext of marriage.
It is further case of prosecution that the prosecutrix had roamed along with the applicant for about 4 years without offering any resistance and when he denied to marry her, she lodged a report.
3. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated and he has not committed any crime.
He submits that the FIR was registered on 04.01.2022 after about 4 years and 5 months of the alleged incident dated 15.08.2017.

He further submits that there was love affair between the applicant and so called victim/prosecutrix and at present the age of the victim is 22 Shubham Choudhary vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79632134/
1 years, a major lady, capable of understanding her well being.

sentences.text: He submits that no offence under POCSO is made out because on the date of lodging the FIR, the prosecutrix was major.

Lastly, he submits that the medical report also does not support the case of the prosecution and the applicant is in jail since 07.09.2022, charge sheet has been filed and the trial is likely to take sometime and therefore, the applicant may be granted bail.

4. On the other hand, State counsel opposes the bail application and submits that on the first date of commission of the offence in the year 2017, the prosecutrix was minor and therefore offence under POCSO is made out.
He further submits that from the statement of the prosecutrix, prima facie case is made out against the applicant and therefore the applicant is not entitled for bail.

5. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the facts and circumstance of the case, in particular the nature of allegations against the applicant and the fact that the prosecutrix was major and consenting party, without commenting anything on merits, I am inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of applicant executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs. 50,000/- with one surety to the satisfaction of the concerned trial court, he shall be released on bail on the following conditions:
I) he shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such fact to the court.

ii) he shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial, and iii) he shall appear before the trial court on each and every date given to him by the said court till disposal of the trial iv) he shall not involve himself in any offence of similar nature in future or else this order granting bail to the applicant shall automatically stand cancelled without further reference to the Court v) he is restrained from meeting any of the prosecution witness till the conclusion of the trial, if any violation is found and it is reported to the trial court, the trial court would be at liberty to take a decision with regard to cancellation of the bail.
7.
It is made clear that these observations are only for the purposes of deciding the bail application.
The trial court shall decide the case on its merits without being influenced by any observation made hereinabove.
